cases.name: c0_c1_controls_removed
cases.note: Vertical tab, form feed, the file/group/record separators and NEL are controls, so they are removed and counted like any other control. Only tab, newline and carriage return survive.

cases.name: unicode_line_separators_left_to_the_caller
cases.note: U+2028/U+2029 are separators, not hidden characters, and Strip must NOT rewrite them: U+2028 is legal inside a JSON string and turning it into a raw newline there produces invalid JSON. Folding belongs to whichever layer does line-based quoting or interpolates into a structured document (the work brief; Go's Line()/line()). Settled 2026-09-18 by reconciling the Python detector with both Go helpers, which already drew the line here.

cases.name: zwj_between_latin_letters_is_stripped
cases.note: The security-relevant half of the joiner question, and every implementation agrees: a joiner between Latin letters renders as nothing, so it both hides text from a reader and makes two distinct strings (prod-1 and prod<ZWJ>-1) look identical. Joiners inside emoji and inside joining scripts are the separate question in profile_notes.

cases.name: joiner_between_joining_script_letters_survives
cases.note: Persian needs ZWNJ to shape words, so stripping it mangles a customer's own name in the text we quote back to them. The rule is the source of truth's (cluster isJoiningScriptLetter): keep a joiner between two LETTERS that are not Latin, Greek or Cyrillic. See the known_limit in profile_notes for where that rule does not reach.

cases.name: indic_joiner_after_the_virama_survives
cases.note: The real Devanagari sequence: ka + virama + ZWJ + sha, where the joiner forces a half-form. The rule's look-behind skips combining marks for exactly this reason, so the consonant, not the virama, is what the letter test sees.

cases.name: joiner_before_a_combining_mark_is_stripped
cases.note: The reversed ordering, ka + ZWJ + virama + sha, is not a sequence any Indic text produces, so the joiner has no shaping job and is stripped. Pinning both orderings is what stops a look-behind change from silently flipping either one. My own first attempt at the Devanagari case used this ordering and I wrongly concluded from the failure that no implementation handled Indic at all; the ankra-cli fork caught it by reading the Go.

cases.name: emoji_zwj_family_survives
cases.note: A real ZWJ sequence. Stripping these joiners would corrupt ordinary user text.

cases.name: emoji_variation_selector_survives
cases.note: U+FE0F after a symbol is emoji presentation, not smuggling; skin tone modifiers likewise.

cases.name: rgi_subdivision_flags_survive
cases.note: The only three subdivision flags with recommended emoji presentation.

cases.name: flag_carve_out_is_a_closed_list_not_a_shape
cases.note: REGRESSION: accepting any short lowercase tag run after U+1F3F4 smuggled words. 'close' is five letters and a black flag is an ordinary character. Caught in cluster PR #3273 review, 2026-09-17.

cases.name: flag_base_with_long_tag_run
cases.note: A long run is not a flag under any reading.

cases.name: ordinary_text_untouched
cases.note: Accented Latin, CJK, Arabic, the micro sign and an em dash are ordinary content. A false positive here corrupts real customer text.

profile_notes.question: ZWJ/ZWNJ between characters of a script that uses joiners (Arabic, Persian, Indic, and others)
profile_notes.status: SETTLED as the display rule and now ASSERTED above. cluster enginekit/hiddenunicode is the source of truth and keeps them (isJoiningScriptLetter: any letter that is not Latin, Greek or Cyrillic); portal's util keeps them via a named script list; the Python detector was brought onto the cluster rule on 2026-09-18.
profile_notes.remaining_non_conformers: ankra-cli internal/hiddenunicode and agent internal/hiddenunicode drop every joiner except between emoji, so they still reshape Persian and Indic words. Tracked as ankra-4r75g.13; both are in review as PR #353 and PR #161.
profile_notes.known_narrower_variant: portal's named list is narrower than cluster's denylist, so a joiner between two CJK characters is kept by cluster and dropped by portal. Harmless today (CJK does not use joiners for shaping) and not worth a third rule, but it is why this case uses Persian and Devanagari rather than CJK.
profile_notes.beware: portal's first attempt used \p{L} for 'joining script', which includes Latin, so de<ZWJ>lete still survived. The zwj_between_latin_letters_is_stripped case above is what catches getting it wrong.
profile_notes.combining_marks: the look-behind skips Mn/Mc, because an Indic joiner follows the virama rather than the consonant, so ka+virama+ZWJ+sha is kept and the reversed ordering is stripped. Both are asserted above. An earlier note here claimed the opposite - that every implementation reshaped Indic conjuncts - which was wrong: I had written the test vector in the reversed ordering and drew the conclusion from my own bad vector rather than from the code.
